title: Lipstick Set Drawer Box: A Practical Buying Guide
seoTitle: Lipstick Set Drawer Box Buying Guide | MTT
summary: Plan a drawer box for a lipstick collection: measure each tube, choose insert access, review the drawer and sample the full pack.
intro: A lipstick set drawer box must let the customer slide open the tray and remove individual tubes without disturbing the rest. Start with closed products and their caps, then define the insert and tray clearance together. A physical sample is needed to check the loaded drawer.
cta: Send the number of lipsticks per set, closed tube dimensions and weight, the desired presentation order, quantity per design and destination. MTT can review drawer and insert options for orders from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Map the collection before choosing the box

List each lipstick with its cap fitted, including labels, irregular bases and decorative features. Measure the maximum length, width and height rather than assuming all shades use identical containers. Note whether the customer should pick up tubes by the body or by an end.

The lip colour wardrobe drawer-box design presents five slim positions in a sliding tray. It is a packaging design reference; the image does not establish an order, production tolerance or shipping performance.

Size the row and check the sliding tray

Illustrative calculation: five positions each 25 mm wide with four 3 mm separating spaces occupy 137 mm (5 × 25 + 4 × 3). This excludes end margins, insert edges, material build-up and assembly clearance. The figures are a planning exercise, not a production specification or an MTT project measurement.

Review the inner tray height with the tallest capped tube, the sleeve clearance with the finished wrap, and any pull or finger notch. A tray that slides comfortably empty may behave differently when loaded. Review the drawer clearance guide for the sleeve-to-tray decision.
Approve the physical sample and shipping pack

Load every position, slide the drawer open and closed, remove each tube and inspect the decoration for rubbing. Check whether any insert shifts as the tray moves and whether the pull remains accessible. Agree the sample type and record the final artwork, paper and insert revision before approving production.

Presentation and parcel protection are separate checks. FedEx describes individual cushioning and an outer protective box for fragile products; carrier requirements depend on the shipment.[1] ISTA explains that its procedures evaluate a specific packaged-product system, not a material in isolation.[2] No transit performance can be inferred from a rendering.

Provide the five product measurements if they differ, packed weight, artwork, desired opening sequence, order quantity and destination. Ask whether the box, insert, sample, tooling, packing and freight are separate line items. Compare suppliers on the same specification and quantities rather than the price alone.

1. FedEx Canada: Learn to Pack and Order Supplies, reviewed 12 November 2026. Carrier guidance varies by route and service.
  2. ISTA: Can I certify an individual packaging material?, reviewed 12 November 2026. Testing relates to a specific packaged-product system.
